quick: Allergic rhinitis: 1 mg twice daily (max 6 mg/day); urticaria/angioedema: 2 mg twice daily
Use only if clearly needed; avoid near term
No specific adjustment defined; use caution
summary: Clemastine is a first-generation (ethanolamine) H1-antihistamine used to relieve allergic rhinitis symptoms (sneezing, rhinorrhea, itching, lacrimation) and mild uncomplicated urticaria and angioedema (at the 2 mg level). It is sedating and anticholinergic, contraindicated in nursing mothers and newborns/premature infants, and should be used cautiously with narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, and in the elderly.
indications: Relief of symptoms of allergic rhinitis (sneezing, rhinorrhea, pruritus, lacrimation)
Relief of mild uncomplicated allergic skin manifestations of urticaria and angioedema (at the 2 mg dosage level)

dosage.d: 1 mg twice daily, increase as needed (max 6 mg/day)

admin: Individualize dose to the needs and response of the patient
May be taken with or without food
Avoid in newborn, premature infants and nursing mothers
moa: Clemastine is a first-generation ethanolamine antihistamine that competitively antagonizes histamine at H1 receptors, reducing histamine-mediated effects (vasodilation, increased capillary permeability, pruritus, sneezing). It crosses the blood-brain barrier (causing sedation) and has anticholinergic activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to clemastine or similar antihistamines

preg: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and benefit outweighs risk. First-generation antihistamines are generally avoided near term.
lact: Contraindicated in nursing mothers - antihistamines carry a higher risk for infants, especially newborns and premature infants, and may be excreted in breast milk.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is defined; use with caution.
hepatic: Use with caution; data are limited.

major: MAO inhibitors (prolong and intensify anticholinergic effects)
moderate: CNS depressants - hypnotics, sedatives, tranquilizers (additive sedation)
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress skin test (allergy) reactions - discontinue several days before testing

monitoring: Degree of sedation and ability to perform alert tasks
Anticholinergic effects (urinary retention, dry mouth, constipation)
Blood pressure and dizziness in the elderly
counsel: May cause marked drowsiness - do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you
Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, prostate problems, or difficulty urinating
Report difficulty urinating or unusual restlessness
pk: Plasma peak ~2-4 hours; peak effect ~5-7 hours
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light
pearls: First-generation, sedating antihistamine - prominent drowsiness and anticholinergic effects
Urticaria/angioedema indication is only at the 2 mg dosage level
Contraindicated in nursing mothers and in newborn/premature infants
Discontinue antihistamines several days before allergy skin testing to avoid false-negative results
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered, unless it is almost time for the next dose - then skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose ranges from CNS depression (sedation, coma) to stimulation (especially in children - excitation, hallucinations, seizures), plus anticholinergic effects (fixed dilated pupils, flushing, hyperthermia, dry mouth, tachycardia). Treatment is supportive; control seizures and hyperthermia and monitor cardiac and respiratory status.
